title: Consolidated decision entries for one theme
description: One object per theme slice. Emitted by a consolidation session (S10b..S10l) reading exactly one slice from extractions/slices/, and consumed by S10z, which numbers the entries and renders docs/DECISIONS.md. FROZEN: consolidation sessions adapt to this schema, never the reverse. The chain uid -> quote -> distilled line must survive into the finished document, so that every claim in the record stays checkable without re-opening the union.

theme.description: Theme name, exactly as in the slice file.

slice_primary_total.description: Count of decisions in this slice with placement='primary', copied from the slice's n_primary. Do not recount. The coverage gate is checked against it.

entries.description: The consolidated record for this theme. Expect roughly one entry per 5-10 source decisions: extraction was deliberately finer-grained than the finished document.

slug.description: Stable kebab-case handle, unique within the theme, e.g. 'route-on-ours-union-theirs'. Entries carry NO D-nn number: numbering is global and only S10z can assign it. Cross-references between entries use slugs until then.

title.description: Declarative one-liner, no trailing period. This becomes the entry heading.

date_from.description: Date the decision was made. When merging several source decisions, the EARLIEST — when the position was first taken, not when it was restated.

date_to.description: Only for a decision argued across several days, e.g. a refutation that accumulated evidence. Null for a single-day decision — do not pad a range to look deliberate.

decision.description: What was decided, stated so it is actionable without reading the sources. Renders as the **Decision.** paragraph.

rationale_recorded.description: Did any source decision actually state a reason? If every source has rationale_recorded=false, this is false and rationale MUST be null. Consolidation is where a tidy after-the-fact justification is most tempting; a missing reason is a finding about the record, not a gap to fill.

rationale.description: Why, AS ARGUED AT THE TIME, merged from the sources' rationales. Renders as the **Why.** paragraph. Never a later or better reason than the one given.

status.description: State as of 2026-07-25. adopted: in force. superseded: replaced by a later decision (name it in superseded_by). reversed: undone, not replaced. open: live question, no ruling. proposed: recommended in the transcript with no visible ratification — 143 source decisions carry this; resolving it needs the code or a later transcript, so leave it proposed rather than guessing. abandoned: dropped without a ruling.

status_note.description: Required when status is 'proposed' or 'open': what would settle it, and where to look. Null otherwise.

supersedes.description: Slugs of entries this replaces, or a plain description when the thing replaced is a plan document rather than an entry.

superseded_by.description: Slug of the entry that replaced this one. If that entry is in a different theme, also add a cross_theme record — this theme cannot see it to verify.

sources.description: Every union uid this entry consolidates, e.g. 'a:20b53f98-04'. This is the provenance chain and the coverage gate: each primary uid in the slice must appear here or in not_promoted. Citing an 'also' uid owned by another theme is fine and does not count toward coverage.

evidence.description: Quotes carried into the finished document, so a reader can check the entry against the transcript without the union. Normally drawn from the sources' own quotes. Two when the rationale is the load-bearing part.

text.description: VERBATIM substring of the distilled file, machine-checked exactly as in extraction. May span a line break (PROTOCOL §8 Amendment 2). No paraphrase, no tidied typo, no ellipsis.

file.description: Distilled filename, e.g. 2026-05-18_20b53f98.txt. Required because one entry may merge sources from several transcripts.

artifacts.description: Commit shas, file paths, ISSUES numbers, report directories the decision names. Renders into **Source.**

actors.description: Who made the call. Feeds the thesis contribution-delineation table, so it is load-bearing. Where sources disagree, do NOT take a majority: use 'joint' if options were put and Ali picked, 'unclear' if the record genuinely does not say, and explain in actors_note.

actors_note.description: Required when the source decisions disagree about actors. Null otherwise.

corroboration.description: From the §6 two-pass run, via each source's corroboration.status. 'both' = every source was found independently by both passes. 'single-pass' = every source came from only one pass, so the entry rests on weaker evidence and S11 should sample it preferentially. 'mixed' = some of each.

provenance.description: Derived from the sources' era and checked against it, not declared. 'chat' when every source is transcript-era (uid a:/b:) — the reasoning is what was argued at the time. 'reconstructed' when every source is pre-transcript (uid preA:/preB:), rebuilt from commit messages and planning documents, where the deliberation is lost. 'mixed' for both. Renders as the v1 provenance tag.

confidence.description: low = the sources support this entry only loosely, or merging them was a judgment call that could reasonably have gone another way. Low-confidence entries are kept and flagged for S11, not dropped.

not_promoted.description: Every primary uid in the slice that did NOT become part of an entry, with a one-line reason: a restatement of another decision, a status update, too minor to carry, or superseded within the slice. This is the consolidation analogue of extraction's near_misses — it is how S11 audits the threshold, and it is half of the coverage gate. An empty list on a large slice reads as an unexamined threshold, not a clean one.

cross_theme.description: Relationships this session can see but cannot resolve, because the other end is in a slice it did not read. S10z reconciles these. Raise one whenever an entry supersedes, is superseded by, contradicts, or duplicates something you believe sits in another theme — including for the 'also'-placed decisions, which exist precisely because they straddle a boundary.

other_theme.description: Suspected theme at the other end, null if unknown.

other_uid.description: The union uid at the other end, when known.

relation.description: Direction from this theme's entry to the other end.

notes.description: Anything S10z needs: a merge you were unsure about, a decision that clearly continues into another theme, a coverage shortfall and why.
